name: ES vs CL Rolling Correlation — US/EU Overlap Session
description: 60-bar rolling Pearson correlation between ES (S&P 500 E-Mini) and CL (Crude Oil WTI) futures on 5-minute bars, restricted to the US/EU overlap session (8:00–11:30am ET). Returns are bar-to-bar simple returns. Shows how the ES/CL relationship evolves over time, flags extreme correlation regimes (|corr| > 0.7), and summarizes the distribution of correlation values.
source:
# =============================================================================
# ES vs CL ROLLING CORRELATION — US/EU OVERLAP SESSION (8:00–11:30am ET)
# =============================================================================
# Question: How does the intraday ES/CL correlation evolve over time, and
#   what does its distribution look like?
#
# Method:
#   - 5-min bars for both ES and CL futures (continuation, liquidity-based roll)
#   - Session filter: 8:00–11:30am ET (US/EU overlap window)
#   - Bar-to-bar simple returns, NaN outside session
#   - rolling_corr(window=60) — DropNulls policy skips off-session bars
#   - Extreme regime: |corr| > 0.7
#
# Outputs:
#   1. xy_lines  — correlation over time (context + evolution)
#   2. histogram — distribution shape (can you trust the typical reading?)
#   3. event_marker — extreme correlation events (|corr| > 0.7)
# =============================================================================

# --- Data: ES continuation ---
es_raw = market_data_source(timeframe=5Min)()
es = futures_continuation(
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.LiquidityBased,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.BackwardRatio
)(es_raw.o, es_raw.h, es_raw.l, es_raw.c, es_raw.v, es_raw.oi, es_raw.s)

# --- Data: CL continuation (reference) ---
cl_raw = reference_futures(ticker='CL')()
cl = futures_continuation(
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.LiquidityBased,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.BackwardRatio
)(cl_raw.o, cl_raw.h, cl_raw.l, cl_raw.c, cl_raw.v, cl_raw.oi, cl_raw.s)

# --- Session filter: 8:00–11:30am ET (US/EU overlap) ---
# session_window.active = True on bars within the window
overlap_session = session_window(
    session=Session(start='08:00', end='11:30', tz='America/New_York')
)(es.o, es.h, es.l, es.c, es.v)

# --- Bar-to-bar simple returns ---
es_ret_raw = returns(period=1)(es.c)
cl_ret_raw = returns(period=1)(cl.c)

# --- Restrict returns to session window only ---
# NaN outside session; rolling_corr DropNulls policy skips those bars
es_ret = where(overlap_session.active, es_ret_raw)
cl_ret = where(overlap_session.active, cl_ret_raw)

# --- 60-bar rolling Pearson correlation (session bars only) ---
corr = rolling_corr(window=60, method=CorrelationMethod.pearson)(es_ret, cl_ret)

# --- Extreme regime flags ---
is_strong_positive = corr > 0.7
is_strong_negative = corr < -0.7
is_extreme = is_strong_positive or is_strong_negative

# Direction label for event card badge
corr_direction = 1.0 if is_strong_positive else -1.0 if is_strong_negative else 0.0

bar_ts = index()

# =============================================================================
# OUTPUT 1: Correlation time series — how does the relationship evolve?
# =============================================================================
xy_lines(
    title='Does ES Track Crude Oil During the US/EU Overlap?',
    category='ES vs CL Correlation',
    order=1,
    y_axis_label='60-Bar Rolling Correlation (Session Bars)',
    y_axis_format=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
    y_axis_dp=2,
    y_plot_bands=PlotBandSchema(bands=[
        PlotBand(from=0.7, to=1.0, color=Color.Blue, opacity=0.08, label='Strong Positive'),
        PlotBand(from=-1.0, to=-0.7, color=Color.Red, opacity=0.08, label='Strong Negative')
    ]),
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0.0, color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash, title='Zero'),
        ReferenceLine(value=0.7, color=Color.Blue, dash_style=DashStyle.Dot, title='+0.7'),
        ReferenceLine(value=-0.7, color=Color.Red, dash_style=DashStyle.Dot, title='-0.7')
    ]),
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name='ES/CL Correlation (60-bar)', color=Color.Blue)
    ])
)(bar_ts, corr)

# =============================================================================
# OUTPUT 2: Distribution histogram — what is the typical correlation reading?
# =============================================================================
histogram(
    title='Distribution of ES/CL Correlation Values',
    category='ES vs CL Correlation',
    order=2,
    bins=40,
    fill_color=Color.Blue,
    fill_opacity=0.7,
    show_analytics=True,
    x_axis_label='60-Bar Rolling Correlation',
    y_axis_label='Frequency',
    x_axis_format=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
    x_axis_dp=2,
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0.0, color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash, title='Zero'),
        ReferenceLine(value=0.7, color=Color.Blue, dash_style=DashStyle.Dot, title='+0.7 Threshold'),
        ReferenceLine(value=-0.7, color=Color.Red, dash_style=DashStyle.Dot, title='-0.7 Threshold')
    ])
)(corr)

# =============================================================================
# OUTPUT 3: Event markers — extreme correlation regimes (|corr| > 0.7)
# =============================================================================
event_marker(
    schema=EventMarkerSchema(
        title='Extreme ES/CL Correlation',
        icon=Icon.ActivityIcon,
        schemas=[
            ColumnSpec(
                title='Correlation',
                type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                dp=3,
                card_slot=CardSlot.Hero
            ),
            ColumnSpec(
                title='Direction',
                type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                dp=0,
                card_slot=CardSlot.PrimaryBadge
            ),
            ColumnSpec(
                table_is_filter=True,
                table_visible=False
            )
        ]
    )
)(corr, corr_direction, is_extreme)
